- If sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 1–3% for next period.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is rising, model often underestimates upside; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% if sentiment turns positive.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above peak or use mean-reversion anchor.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, model tends to smooth too much; allow 1–2% volatility buffer in forecast.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70), model often fails to recognize it; reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per day.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period volatility; add 0.5–1.5% upward adjustment if sentiment is neutral or bullish in last 3–5 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values (neutral or negative), model tends to ignore trend; apply slight upward bias if price is trending up, or downward if trending down.
